last_3_hypotheses: Hallucination rate in tool-use outputs drops as the dialog history accumulates more verified tool-call/result pairs the model can copy structural patterns from.
PD strategy switching from TFT to all-D after a single defection is more common when the system prompt names "tit-for-tat" explicitly, suggesting prompt leakage shapes the learned policy.
ChromaDB k-NN queries against papers_recent return more diverse top-5 results when the query embedding has L2 norm > 1.2.
proposed_hypothesis_text: Longer dialog history reduces hallucination rate because the model has more concrete examples of valid outputs in its working context and tends to copy structure from those rather than fabricate.
rationale: Same claim with the same mechanism (model copies structural patterns from in-context examples to reduce hallucination). The original is more specific (tool-use, verified pairs); the proposed is more general (dialog history, valid outputs). A meta-reviewer should recognize the proposed as a generalization of the original — duplicate, not novel contribution.
